model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) percentage for five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on the x-axis using a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale from 40% to 65%. The 'Base' method is shown as a black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 38.5% and rising to about 44% before leveling off. The 'MEND' method, represented by a brown line with diamond markers, begins near 44% and increases to around 56.5%. The 'FT' method, shown as a blue line with triangular markers, starts at about 40% and rises to approximately 47.5%. The 'MEMIT' method, depicted with a purple line and circular markers, begins at roughly 44% and increases to about 54.5%. The 'ROME' method, shown as a green line with square markers, starts at approximately 51% and rises steadily to about 65.5%.
